subject: .skills/fleet-add-capability
verdict: Lean, well-structured skill with clean architecture and determinism boundaries, but missing working-state and degradation paths expected of a multi-turn file-producing workflow.
summary: The skill's primary strength is its concise encoding of repo-specific conventions (sync-wave contract, OperatorPolicy pattern, lifecycle-group decomposition, env-var-vs-overlay decision criteria) in under 1500 tokens. Its primary opportunity is adding the multi-turn patterns its sibling skills already carry: a memlog for decision persistence, a fast path for experts, and fallback routes when scripts or web search fail.

themes.title: Multi-turn resilience
themes.root_cause: The skill accumulates decisions across turns (capability name, method, parts, waves, targets) but has no mechanism to persist them — if context compacts or the session resumes, earlier decisions are lost.
themes.action: Add a memlog (matching sibling skills fleet-add-cluster and fleet-add-node) that captures each decision as it lands, enabling resume and audit.

themes.title: Expert and automation paths
themes.root_cause: The skill forces all users through the same linear flow regardless of how much information they already have. An expert who provides all inputs upfront still waits through research; an automator cannot invoke it headlessly at all.
themes.action: Gate on input completeness: if the user supplies method + parts + target in the invocation, skip research and confirm; if a structured block is provided with --headless, produce files without interaction.

themes.title: Failure path coverage
themes.root_cause: Two hard dependencies (resolve_repo_structure.py, web search) have no fallback. The skill dead-ends if either fails rather than asking the user to supply what the tool could not.
themes.action: Add graceful degradation: fall back to manual component listing if the script fails; ask the user to paste docs or describe the method if web search returns nothing; confirm product identity before committing to research.

themes.title: Natural-behavior ceremony
themes.root_cause: A few instructions describe behaviors a capable model would perform unprompted (showing summaries, reminding about .gitignore, awaiting confirmation before multi-file writes).
themes.action: Trim Post-Generation to the fleet-explain-component cross-reference; collapse Research bullets to a single sentence naming the key dimensions.

strengths: Excellent token efficiency — 1411 tokens encoding deep repo-specific knowledge that a model cannot infer
Clean intelligence-placement boundary: deterministic parsing in scripts, judgment in the prompt
Sound progressive disclosure — everything inline, nothing carved unnecessarily, all paths resolve
Installation-method classification table is the highest-leverage content: it prevents the most common error (wrong component pattern for the deployment mechanism)
Gotchas section encodes institutional knowledge with real consequences (OperatorPolicy not Subscription, wave 6 reservation, namespace placement)

recommendations.action: Add a memlog strategy matching the sibling skills — init on activation, append decisions at each phase gate (research confirmed, structure proposed, files generated, wiring applied)
Add input-completeness gate: if method + lifecycle + target are present in invocation, skip research and jump to structure proposal confirmation
Add fallback paths for script failure (manual ls + user listing) and web-search failure (user pastes docs or describes method)
Add product-identity confirmation before committing to web research, and orientation context when invoked without args
Trim Post-Generation to the fleet-explain-component offer; collapse Research sub-bullets to one sentence

journeys.name: First-timer without args
journeys.steps: Gets blank prompt with no guidance — needs orientation (enhancement-5)

journeys.name: Expert with full spec
journeys.steps: Forced through redundant web research — needs fast path (enhancement-2, enhancement-6)

journeys.name: Air-gapped environment
journeys.steps: Web search fails with no fallback — needs degradation path (enhancement-3)

experience.headless: Not currently supported — blocks automation use cases (enhancement-2)

findings.title: Post-Generation section is mostly natural model behavior
findings.evidence: "Show a summary of everything created" and "Remind the user to add secrets to .gitignore" are default behaviors a capable model would perform after generating multiple files. Only the fleet-explain-component offer is novel.
findings.recommendation: Collapse to: 'After generation, offer to run `fleet-explain-component <name>` for verification.'
findings.proposed_smallest: Offer to run `fleet-explain-component <name>` to verify the generated readme matches reality.
findings.predicted_delta: Saves ~60 tokens. The summary and .gitignore reminders would still happen naturally.

findings.title: Research bullet list partially redundant
findings.evidence: Bullets for namespaces, CRDs, and dependencies are standard items any model researching an operator install would surface. The guiding bullet is the installation method classification.
findings.recommendation: Trim to one sentence: 'Research the product's OpenShift installation method (OLM, helm, raw manifests), namespace requirements, and dependencies.'
findings.proposed_smallest: Research the product's OpenShift install method and dependencies.

findings.title: Explicit confirmation gate is natural multi-file behavior
findings.evidence: 'Present the proposed structure to the user for confirmation before generating any files.' — models already gate multi-file creation behind user approval.
findings.recommendation: Could be cut; ~15 tokens saved with virtually zero quality difference.

findings.title: Hardcoded readme template path could be a scalar
findings.evidence: The skill references `{fleet-common}/references/readme-template.md` as the template. An org with different doc standards would need to fork the skill.
findings.recommendation: If customize.toml is ever added, expose as `readme_template` scalar. Not urgent — the template lives in fleet-common and can be edited directly.

findings.title: Post-generation is an on_complete hook candidate
findings.evidence: The skill produces files then suggests follow-ups — the classic 'produces artifact and stops' pattern for on_complete.
findings.recommendation: If customize.toml is added, consider `on_complete = "fleet-explain-component"`. Low priority.

findings.title: Add Working-state-across-turns
findings.evidence: Multi-turn skill accumulating decisions (name, method, parts, waves, targets) with no persistence mechanism. Sibling skills use memlogs.
findings.recommendation: Add memlog init on activation and append at each phase gate (research, proposal, generation, wiring).

findings.title: Add Three-mode-architecture
findings.evidence: Only supports Guided mode. No Headless for CI/automation, no fast-path for experts who already know the classification.
findings.recommendation: Add input-completeness gate: if all fields present, skip to generation; if --headless flag, produce files without interaction.

findings.title: Add Graceful-degradation
findings.evidence: Two hard dependencies (resolve_repo_structure.py, web search) have no fallback path.
findings.recommendation: Fall back to manual ls for script failure; ask user to paste docs for search failure.

findings.title: Strengthen Intent-before-ingestion
findings.evidence: 'add vault' could mean HashiCorp Vault, Vault Secrets Operator, or External Secrets with Vault backend. Research starts before confirming which product.
findings.recommendation: Add brief product-identity confirmation before web research.

findings.title: Add Soft-gate-elicitation for arg-less activation
findings.evidence: When invoked without args, the user gets a blank prompt with no context about existing components or common additions.
findings.recommendation: Present orientation: categories of capabilities, component count, and offer to suggest gaps.

findings.title: Remove over-applied forced research
findings.evidence: Research is mandatory even when the expert user has already provided all classification info.
findings.recommendation: Make research conditional on whether user input already specifies method + lifecycle + target.
